The 32-year-old convicted murderer turned jail escapee until his arrest overnight in Chicago. Authorities around Illinois had been looking for Taylor since early Wednesday, when he jumped a correctional officer at Kankakee's Jerome Combs Detention Center, then took off with the guard's uniform and SUV. Surveillance video was the last officials saw of Taylor until just before midnight Friday, in Chicago. "They saw a guy that matched the description," Bukowski said.

Prince Harry of Britain, age 30, is going to spend time in Australia as his military career comes to an end. The prince is scheduled to arrive on Monday for a four-week stay with the Australian armed forces. The Australian Defence Forces announced on Thursday that Harry will live and work alongside Australian Army colleagues in several regments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. A spokesman said that he has spent time with Australian troops several times during his 10-year military career.

The Florida Attorney General’s office announced on Thursday that three men have been charged with plotting to kill a former prisoner who was about to be released. Two current Florida prison guards and one former guard-in-training are the suspects. They used their jobs to guard Florida prisons, but now they are the ones in jail. The FBI informant met the men—Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42— after infiltrating a branch of the KKK: the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, CNN affiliate WJXT reported. Driver told the informant that he had gotten into a fight with the inmate and that he and Moran wanted him "six feet under," according to court documents.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) — A week of intense negotiations in Lausanne ended on Thursday with a framework agreement between Iran and the P5+1 (a group of world powers) regarding Iran's nuclear program. The success of this agreement remains to be seen. The parties have until the end of June to work out the details and put the plan to paper. But the talks this week were, nevertheless, historic, particularly for the otherwise frozen U.S.-Iranian relationship. But that's not to say they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an improvised bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle close to the city of Garowe in northeastern Somalia. The attack killed six people, including four aid workers from UNICEF, the international children's agency. Somalia's President called this "an attack against the future of our country." The attack came after another incident on Sunday, when three African Union soldiers died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for Monday's attack, which occurred about 8 a.m in the administrative capital of the autonomous Puntland region, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will spend four weeks working with the Australian military. Before starting his duty, the 30-year prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He stopped at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier to pay his respects. A crowd of people gathered outside the memorial. Some took photos of the prince. One boy held a sign that said, “Red Heads Rule!” to celebrate the Harry’s red hair. During his time in Australia, Harry will work and live with soldiers in the Australian Army. He will serve in several regments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. The Australian Defence Forces said this plan last week.

Australia, a close ally of the United States, has agreed to share some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the deal is "an informal arrangement" with a focus on tracking Australians who go to Iraq to fight for ISIS. But one Australian lawmaker reportedly described the move as "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview released Monday that Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

Initial tests on the flight data recorder (called the "black box") from Germanwings Flight 9525, which crashed in the French Alps on March 24, show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally used the controls to make the plane dive faster. according to the French air accident investigation agency, the BEA. The black box was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had been searching the mountainside for days. A statement from the BEA on Friday said its teams had immediately begun to investigate its contents.

The crew of a fishing boat named the Thunder was rescued by conservationists, who had been chasing them for 110 days. The chase went from the waters near Antarctica to the coast of West Africa. The boat was an alleged poaching vessel. The conservationists are from the group Sea Shepherd. They had been following the Thunder since their ship, the Bob Barker, saw it in the Southern Ocean several months ago. The Thunder is subject of an Interpol "purple notice" for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes. The chase ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

16-year-old Jason Zobott goes to Huntley High School in suburban Chicago at 7:30 in the morning, like most students. But what he does during the day is unusual. He is in a special class at the school that mixes online learning with normal classroom teaching. One-third of the 2700 students are in this class. By 2025, the school wants most students to be in this class. "It is easy to do my work online," said Zobott, a top student who has many activities outside of school. "I can learn by myself."

Days after a terrible Al-Shabaab attack in Garissa, Kenya, the Kenyan military launched airstrikes against the terrorist group in Somalia. A military source confirmed this. The source said the strikes were not revenge for last week’s massacre at Garissa University College, which killed almost 150 people. “The latest attack of Al-Shabaab bases by the Kenya military is part of the ongoing operations that started in 20 2011. It is not a retaliation to the Garissa attack. The operation has been ongoing,” the military source said Monday. It is customary for Kenyan military sources not to give their names to media.

Pope Francis gave a traditional speech after Easter Mass to remind the world that the Vatican is its own country and that he acts as a moral leader. He spoke about the pain people are feeling in current wars and asked for an end to violence everywhere. He specifically asked for the fighting in Iraq and Syria to stop and for help to reach those who need it. He said, "May the international community not stand by before the immense humanitarian tragedy unfolding in these countries and the drama of the numerous refugees," he said in his "urbi et orbi" address, Latin for "to the city (Rome) and to the world.

On Wednesday afternoon, Duke University students and faculty members marched across campus, chanting “We are not afraid. We stand together.” This happened after a rope noose was found hanging from a tree. Duke officials asked anyone with information about the rope noose, which was found near a student center at 2 a.m., to call campus police. Photos of the noose prompted outrage from the community as they were passed along on social media. At a forum held on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was hung, hundreds of people gathered.

Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, a 29-year U.S. citizen with alleged ties to al Qaeda, appeared in court on Thursday without entering a plea. He is charged with conspiring to provide material support to terrorists. Al Farekh was deported from Pakistan to the United States. He is accused of plotting to fight against American forces abroad, according to a complaint unsealed in U. States District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn. "This is news for celebration," said CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd.

Sanaa, Yemen (CNN) — A Saudi border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants in Yemen this week, the state-run Saudi Press Agency reported on Thursday. This is the first publicly known military death for Saudi Arabia since it started airstrikes against rebels in its southern neighbor, Yemen. The fight happened on Wednesday night at the border in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Press Agency reported that militants in a mountain area on the Yemen side shot at Saudi border troops, who then shot back. The guard, identified as Corporant Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki, was killed. 10 other people were hurt, but their injuries were not life-threatening, the Saudi media outlet said.

The writer feels nervous about going to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. Because they are the only Gulf national on the CNN team, people expect them to know about camel racing, which is an old tradition in the area. Even though they tried to wear a kandora, a traditional dress from the UAE, they still feel like an outsider because of their modern way of life. A friendly farm owner shows them into the majlis, a place where camel owners meet. The big room looks like a fancy theater. The camel owners sit on the floor, eating a'aish, a traditional Arabic dish made of fish and rice, which is placed in front of them. The people are talking loudly and excitedly.

Havana, Cuba (CNN) – Charlie Hill sits in a dark bar on a bright, sunny day in Havana. “Hey man,” he says. His voice is rough from smoking, and he nods to show he knows you have been looking for him. But many people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For 43 years, Cuba has been a safe place for Hill to avoid being charged for killing a New Mexico police officer and hijating an airplane to Havana. Hill, now 65, decided to give CNN an interview after we had spent two years trying to reach him. He wants to talk about how for the first time he is thinking about leaving his safe place and going back to the United States.

Misao Okawa, who was the oldest person in the world according to Guinness World Records, died at age 117. Okawa died Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, Tadahi Uchimura, a city official, told CNN. She leaves behind three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family had a kimono shop in Osaka, Satoshi Yoshioka, an employee at the nursing home where she had lived since 1997, told CNN. "She was a person with mild character, and loved to eat so much. Her favorite food was sushi and udon noodles," Yoshioka said. "She had eaten a lot of cake for her birthday last March 5."

Documents show that the Missouri National Guard used military language, such as "enemy forces" and "ad adversaries," to describe protesters while preparing to go to Ferguson, Missouri, last year to help stop the sporriot. The Guard went to Ferguson to support police officers. Many community leaders and civil rights activists accused the police of using too much force and making the already tense situation worse during protests that happened sporly from August through the end of the year.

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) — Gunners attacked the Somalia’s education ministry in the capital on Tuesday. They came after a suicide car bomb. The attack killed at least 12 people and hurt 16 others, officials said. The Islamist group Al-Shabaab said it was responsible for the attack in central Mogadishu, its spokesman Abu Musab said. The attack started when two suicide bombers blew their car at the entrance of the two-story building that has the Ministry of Education, Culture & Higher Education, Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said. Five gunners then entered the building, shooting people inside, Yusuf said.

One war was enough for 87-year-old Gregory Margolin. He fought in World II as a 16-year-old Jewish soldier in the Soviet Red Army. His family fled while he was fighting the Nazis. Margolin says, “I did not show that I was Jewish. But it did not matter because people were being killed left and right. All around me.” This year, in Ukraine, he found himself again surrounded by war. Margolin was a sniper who rose to be a commander in the army. His old uniform is still adorned with medals from his time in the military. His granddaughter Liora still marvels at his stories from the war. She is amazed that he managed to survive.

It is exactly 365 days since more than 200 Nigerian school girls were taken from their boarding school in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They still are missing. The Nigerian government and the rest of the world have allowed this to happen. We should all feel ashamed. It is shameful that fan criminals can hurt young girls without punishment. It is also shameful that people quickly forget about these terrible events.

Norway is becoming the first country in the world to stop using FM radio. In two years, the switch will be complete. Instead of FM, people will listen to digital radio. This does not mean there will be no radio. Nor Norwegians will just have silence. They will listen to digital radio. Officials in Oslo say many people in this country of 5 million have already made the move. On FM, Norwegians can only find five stations. On the Digital Audio Broadcasting network, there are four times that number. Half the country already listens that way, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

Everyone is big fan of a good comeback story, especially when it involves dinosaurs. A new study suggests that the Brosaurus should get its own name back. It was taken out of science books for over a hundred years. O.C. Marsh first called the Brontosaurus in 1879, after he got 25 crates of bones found at Como Bluff, Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. Similar to, though not as large as the Apatosaurus discovered a couple of years prior, Marsh named the dinosaur, "Brontosaurus," or "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda has offered a reward of 20 kilograms of gold (about $774,000) for anyone who kills or captures two prominent Shia Muslim leaders. The group, known as Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), is fighting for control in Yemen. They released a online news and wanted poster offering the reward for the death or capture of Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh.

The bad news for Rio de Janeiro continues ahead of the 2020 Olympics. after many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. With just over a year to go before the city hosts the Games' rowing and canoe competitions, officials with the legislative assembly of Rio de Janeiro Monday launched an investigation into the causes of death both in the lagoon and in other lakes and bays in the state in which this phenomenon has occurred. The group will work in partnership with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the Secretariat of State for the Environment.

A person has a terrible accident, and they end up in the hospital. Their brain is not working anymore, and they are kept alive by machines. The doctors ask the family to give organs to save eight people. The family is instead asked to give the whole body to save just one person. A person who can't move their body but has a strong mind. This sounds crazy, but Dr. Sergio Canavero, a doctor from Italy, says we are close to doing this. HEAVEN is a short name for a project that puts a head on a new body.

Police say that Anthony Stokes’s story ended in tragedy on Tuesday. It was expected to have a happy ending. Stokes was a teenager who had received a heart transplant. he stole a car, broke into a house, and shot at an elderly woman. He then led police on a fast chase. His car hit a pole, and he died. In 23, his family told the news that a hospital in Atlanta would not give him a new heart. because he had not followed the doctor’s orders. Mark Bell was speaking for the family at that time.

It was before sunrise at Garissa University College in Kenya. most students were still asleep. A few had gotten up early to attend Christian morning prayers. Then the attack began.

 Around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday), the attackers started at the front gates of the school. They used an explosion and gunshots. The attackers continued to shoot as they walked through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, they burst into a room where Christians had gathered and took hostages, said lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, 25, died in police custody 15 days ago after being arrested for a weapons charge. He suffered a severe spinal cord injury, which caused his death. This has caused widespread anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray's death is the latest in a series of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many people have demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral drew civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody. A white casket sat at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore as a gospel choir sang for a large crowd gathered to honor Freddie Gray.

I have been working as a chef since I was 14. I did not start fighting for food policy until much later. It was 2007. I saw a young girl my wife was helping looking through trash for food. This made me start Food Policy Action. I began working on food issues like hunger and factory farms. I was not alone. "The Matrix" was a big help. Dan Swangard is a doctor. He has seen many patients die in hospitals. They were often connected to pain medicine and very worried. He has watched people suffer for weeks or even months while their families stood by, feeling helpless. But now, this is personal for him. In 22013, he was diagnosed with a rare cancer that has spread. Surgeons removed parts of his pancreas and liver, and his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery went well, but Swangard, who is 48, knows the cancer might come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters who were fighting the Houthi rebels and their allies in Aden. The Saudi soldiers were on the ground in non-combat roles, "coordinating and guiding" the battle against Houthi forces and fighters loyal to former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, the source said. They also helped parachute in weapons and communications equipment. Houthi rebels, meanwhile, withdrew from the presidential palace and other key parts of the southern port city of Aden following heavy Saudi airstrikes, according to the source. The withdrawal signaled a reversal from rebel gains the previous day, when Houthi forces seized the presidential palace.

Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy charges Blair for killing her 13 daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9 son, Stephen Gage Berry. According Detroit Police Chief James Craig, the bodies were found wrapped in plastic inside the freezer by a bailiff performing a court ordered eviction on March 24. In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, said that he was “drinking poison” when he agreed to a ceasefire to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had helped define Khomeini’s regime, the Islamic Republic, which he had founded a year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini galvanized the nation, both his supporters and growing opponents, to fight against the enemy. He dragged out the war for eight years, despite Saddam’s willingness to accept a ceasefire, and thus stabilized the foundations of the Islamic Republic. By the time he ended the war, the economy was in shambles, and there was no sign of his die-hard volunteers.

The idea of sustainable development is that unchecked capitalism is too powerful and it is harming itself. Global capitalism is growing very fast, the world economy is now doubling in size every generation. But on a finite Earth, with a billion new people added every 15 years, this growth is now destroying the natural resources and and the social systems that make life good and decent. Sustainable development offers a way out of this growing crisis. The reality is that unchecked capitalism is the economics of greed.

The United States has many benefits from being a space power. Its ability to use space has greatly helped national security, defense, and the economy. The U States military relies on space technology, like intelligence, GPS, and communication satellites, to handle current and future conflicts, fight terrorism, and stop global threats. However, as global threats grow and the need for space access increases, the U States faces a serious problem: it depends too much on Russian technology to meet its national security needs.

On the day before the one-year anniversary of when Boko Haram kidnapped almost 300 school girls in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to the girls on Monday. "Like you, I was a target of militants who did not want girls to go to school," she writes in the letter. The 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner survived an attack by the Taliban, which had singled her out for blogging from Pakistan about the importance of staying in school. In the letter, she calls on the Nigerian government and the international community to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria recently held an election.

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards were killed in fighting with militants near the border with Pakistan. The state-run news agency IRNA reported that Iranian forces killed three of the militants during the fighting on Monday in Negur, a town in the southeast. The news agency cited Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province, who said the militants crossed into the country from Pakistan. Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos is now named TripAdvisor’s number one island in the world. It moved up from second place last year. It passed Ambergris Caye, which was previously the top island. Ambergris Caye had been number one for two years, but it fell out of the top ten this year. Chile will soon recognize same-sex civil unions. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday, making Chile a part of several South American countries that allow these unions. The law takes effect in six months. It gives legal recognition to co relationships between two people of the same sex or between a man and a woman. The government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change. Bachelet said, "This is a concrete step in the drive to end the difference between homosexual and heterosexual couples."

When you next fly to Florida, look out the window. Whether you are visiting family, going to Disney World, or relaxing on the beach, try to get a window seat as you land. and think about the vast swylands below. The Everglades are a powerful example of human mistakes and the price to pay for fixing them. From the air, the area looks like a muddy wasteland full of dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes.

In early April, ISIS militants took over the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. They masked and armed men entered the streets quickly. The camp had already been under attack by Syrian forces for more than two years. The residents were already suffering. Now they faced a new, even more frightening reality. ISIS defeated several other armed groups in the area and took control of almost all of the camp. One resident, who not to be named, told CNN that ISIS killed people in the streets. They caught three people and killed them in front of others.

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors have created a new tool called the "Great Cannon." They previously used the "Great Firewall" to block citizens from reading Western news websites or seeing other content the government disapproved of. But that is no longer enough for them. The Great Cannon attacks servers outside China, including servers in the United States. The study's authors named it the "Great Cannon" because it operates openly. They say this visible attack in another country's borders will likely cause international anger, and Beijing may have expected that.

investigators investigating the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 have not found any evidence showing why the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, committed the act. They have not found any written notes or conversations where he explained his reasons or admitted to any plans. A spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday. However, medical records show that Lubitz was suicidal at one time and received psychotherapy. This was before he ever got his pilot’s license, the spokesman, Christoph Kumpa, said.

The leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels, Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, said on Sunday that he would not give up. A senior Saudi military official claimed that weeks of airstrikes had greatly weakened the Houthi group. The Houthi are a Shiite group. Al-Houthi said in a TV speech that his fighters would not leave the main cities or the government buildings. He said that anyone who thinks they would surrender is dreaming. His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition bombings aimed at pushing back the Houthi, who surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, twenty years ago, Timothy McVeigh drove a large truck bomb and exploded it in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The attack killed 168 men, women and children, injured hundreds more, and remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. The attack's aftermath saw a storm of media coverage with themes such as "attack on the heartland" and America's "lost innocence." In fact, the bombing took the country by surprise. It wasn't simply the scale of the tragedy that drew attention, but the fact that the bombing exposed something new: American citizens targeting their own government with a deadliness hitherto unseen.

If you were worried about something important, would you protest? Would you hold a sign? Would you join a march? How long could you keep trying when no one else seemed to care? When more than 200 Nigerian girls were taken from their school a year ago by Boko Haram fighters, millions of people around the world used social media to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people. — from famous people to world leaders — who showed their anger using #BringBackOurGirls, one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2114, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The spotlight on the campaign faded

Barney Frank, a retired U.S. Congressman, recently spoke to a full audience in Chicago about his 45 years in public service. Frank, was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while in office. He also criticized politicians who hide their sexual identity but vote against gay rights. Frank told a audience member not to worry about a California ballot measure that would allow the killing of gay people, because he was unaware of the measure and said the people supporting it were "crazy."

Al-Shabaab militants attacked Garissa University College in Kenya on Thursday morning. during prayers. The attackers shot people randomly and took hostages before security forces killed them. Nearly 150 people, including students, were killed and dozens more were hurt. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab claimed the attack. The group has done many attacks in the area. They also killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenstone quarry a few months ago. They have recruited some Americans, especially Somali-Americans in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa is celebrating the removal of a statue of a British colonial leader named Cecil Rhodes. This comes after several weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand that the statue be taken down. they said his history is mixed with racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, students showed their opinions in a campaign that began last month. Four weeks later, the hashtag is now #RhodesHas Fallen. The university said on Wednesday that the heritage authority gave them permission to remove the statue from the campus. "These steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the statue while matters concerning its future are resolved," the university said in a statement.

Syria is a terrible place, things are getting worse. The number of people killed has doubled in one year, according to an opposition group. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights says 310,000 people have died since the civil war started. One year ago, the number was 162,402. The year before, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died. The United Nations says more than half of Syrians are so poor they need help to survive. Food rations are being cut because there is not enough money donated.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court looking quiet and shy. but prosecutors say she acted very differently when dealing with a woman she saw as a rival. They say she threatened the woman in a summer phone call. She told the woman, "Leave my man alone." and "Stop looking for him. I know people who can put a bomb where you live." The prosecutors did not think it was a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment. She says she is not guilty. Last December, when she left the court, she and her lawyer would not talk about the case. Ailina Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A door with a graffiti drawing by the British artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday. A Gaza police official told CNN that there was a disagreement about the sale of the door. The owner of the door, Rabea Darduna, filed a complaint with a Gaza court stating that, without realizing its value, he sold the door for just $175 U.S. The iron door will remain in the possession of the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza until a court hearing at a date yet to be determined. When Darduna's Gaza home was destroyed in last summer's war, he says he felt he was left with nothing. Only a doorway and a door.

The Saudi-led coalition’s attacks against Houthi rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The coalition is gaining more control, while many locals are fleeing the violence and the number of deaths is rising, including dozens of civilians. Five days after the first air strikes, a Saudi source said the coalition has destroyed Houthi air defense systems and the systems of supporters of Yemen’s long president, Ali Abdullah Saleh. and made all but a few air bases and runways unusable. The Saudi source said Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all Yemeni ports, allowing only closely watched non-military medical goods to pass its blockade.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands team, strongly criticized his own fans for booing Spanish player Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called them a "disgrace."

Spanish coach Vicente del Bosque used a new lineup for the game at the Amsterdam Arena. Iniesta, who started on the bench, entered the game in the 76th minute and received mixed cheers and boos from the home fans. Stefan de Vrij (center back) and Davy Klaassen (midfielder) scored first-half goals in the morale-boosting victory, but Hiddink was unimpressed with the way Iniesta was treated. Scotland will know on May 21 if their Euro 2016 match against Georgia in September will be played without fans. UEFA has started disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation (GFF) after fans twice invaded the field of play during Sunday's 2-0 defeat by Germany in Tbilisi. European football's governing body is also set to look at charges that allege home fans were guilty of setting off fireworks while a string of safety breaches, including blocked stairs, locked gates and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, will also be investigated. A fan invades the pitch during Georgia's 2-0 defeat by Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi

Football agents were waiting on Wednesday for news about new rules. Starting on April 1, anyone can become a football agent if they pay £500 for the first year. The cost is £250 for each year after. Agents who already have a license are not affected. The FA plans to put a link on their website for registration, but as of 1pm, the link was not there yet. Mel Stein thinks the new rules will "create anarchy". These new rules came after FIFA stopped controlling agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, hasn’t been paid in three months. He had to ask his parents for money to pay his rent. CSKA Sofia has money problems. Uvarenko joined the Bulgarian club in January for 18 months. He likes the fans. The fans are special and they support the team with a strong feeling. Uvarenko told local news on Wednesday, “The no money is the big problem I have at CSKA. I still have no salary. I have been at the club for three months.”

David Moore, 25, was angry because he was stuck in heavy traffic on his way home. He was face-to-face with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Moore punched Cegielka and then broke his car with a hockey stick. young children were watching. Moore said he was having a bad day and lost control of his temper.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This result brought back painful memories of Spain’s terrible performance at the 2014 World Cup. Gerard Pique, a Spanish player, said that coach Vicente del Bosque should not worry too much about losing three friend games in a row. Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena. They kept Spain from scoring in the second half, even though Spain tried hard. The final score was 2-0. This game reminded of the Holland’s 5-1 win against Spain in the group stage of the World Cup in Brazil last year. That loss ended Spain’s six years of control of world soccer.

Police in New York City say that Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany. They are looking for them. A court order says Berger is not allowed to leave the United States with Kaia. Kaia’s father dropped her off at Berger’s home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, on March 21 at 10 a.m. for a weekend visit. On March 22, Berger and Kaia are believed to get on a plane to Germany. This breaks the court order.

A huge fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The flames and thick smoke looked like scenes from a disaster movie. The fire destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches. It happened after days of storms that knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-he-he-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water ran off the slope. Fire investigators have confirmed that the fire was started deliberately and three separate areas of heheath - measuring half a hectare, one hectare and 70 hectares - were destroyed

Last night, across Britain, people celebrating 2012 caused emergency services to receive 600 calls every hour. Paramedics were very busy. In Cambridge, a field hospital from the Terrial Army was opened to help drunk party-goers. The London Ambulance Service said at the peak they were dealing with over 600 calls per hour which is more than three times as many as on a normal night. MANCHESTER: A man is stood slumped over in a doorway as two women walk by as they celebrate the New Year .

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said that his strong mind helped him get better after being left out of the team last December. Mignolet was left out "for an unknown time" by manager Brendan Rodgers in December because he played badly, but he came back quickly after Brad Jones hurt his thigh. The 27-year-old from Belgium told how he tried to stay happy despite being upset about being left out. Simon Mignolet said that his strong mind helped him get better after being left out. Mignolet (second right) made a save from a free kick during a league game against Swansea last month. Mignolet told FourFourTwo: "I was positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell across the southern United States. People went outside to film the unusual weather. A man named Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, recorded video showing ice balls hitting his backyard and spling into his swimming pool. The video shows the hailstones falling fast, many breaking when they hit the ground. Even though it was about 80 degrees, the hard ice lumps did not melt quickly. In just a few seconds, the patio was completely covered in white ice balls.

The crew of a replica pirate ship called the *Liana's Ransom* had to leave the boat because it lost power in bad weather near Maine. Nine people from the ship were saved by Coast Guard life boats on Tuesday. The ship was left floating 30 miles east of Portland. Coast Guard officials said this. Amazing photos of blue glowing algae have taken Australia's east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay on the south coast of New South Wales, showing the bright light on one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson said the sight was a "beautiful supernatural scene" caused by millions of plankton giving off light. A similar display was seen at Sydney's Manly Beach in August 21014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

17-teenager Rahul Kumar was drunk and climbed over a fence into a lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, western India. He ran toward the lions, shouting that he would kill them. He later said he was drunk and thought he had a a good chance against the predators. Zoo security saw him and stopped him.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling from a fifth-story window. He landed on a car parked below. His father thinks the boy fell while sleepwalking. The accident happened last Saturday. A hotel worker across the street heard a loud noise around midnight, which she thought was a car crash.

Drew Miller, a player for the Detroit Red Wings, is happy to be back on the ice. He got a serious cut on his face just one day ago. The injury could have been very bad for his eyes. Miller said he feels very lucky that the skate did not hit his eye. He was wearing a full face mask during practice. The Detroit Free Press reported that Miller had a serious red wound. It needed 50 or 60 stitches to close. The stitches went through many layers of skin. Miller has a scar across his eye now. But he did not lose his eyesight. Another player cut his face.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends next summer, even though Atletico Madrid is thinking about signing him again. He joined Chelsea from Atletico last July and signed a three-year deal, but he has not been able to play well as the left defender at Stamford Bridge. Atletico hopes this might help them get what they want, but Luis said: “I am happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.”

Charlie Sumner, a 20-year-old fan of Reading Football Club, is facing a three-year ban from attending football matches. Sumner went topless onto the field and did four front flips during Reading’s FA Cup quarter-final replay match against Bradford City last month. The match was held at the Madejski Stadium. Reading won 3-0. Sumner was attending his first ever game. He said it was a “brill experience”

A video shows a van carrying football fans swering around a corner near Salé, Morocco. About six men on the roof were thrown off when the van tipped over at high speed. The video was taken by a car following the van. The footage shows the van moving side-to side on a busy road. Scroll down for the video.

England’s Under-17 team plays in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships. The tournament is held in Bulgaria in May. England’s opponents are the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. England’s coach is John Peacock. England is the defending champion because they beat Holland on penalties in last year’s final in Malta. England must beat Holland again to get the quarter-finals. The tournament is bigger now. It has 16 teams instead of 8. This is the first time it has 16 teams. Danny Collinge scored his first goal for England against Norway in the qualifying games.

An elephant was relaxing by a small pool in South Africa’s Kruger National Park with its family. A male buffalo came too close, which annoyed the elephant. The elephant used its trunk to spray water at the buffalo to make it leave, but missed. The elephant tried again, clearly frustrated. Meanwhile, a baby elephant stayed close to its parent for safety while the buffalo drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, 55, has won an eight-year legal fight to clear his name. He was the landlord of a pub called the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. In November 2006, he was convicted for showing a Premier League football game on foreign TV channels without an agreement with the official broadcasters. He says he has paid a heavy price for the long fight to get his conviction quashed and has lost his pub as a result.

The Irish Football Association (IFA) wants to make sure that the game against Romania in June can still happen. The team plays at Windsor Park in Belfast. There was a problem with the building. Cr were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning. The area was closed. experts looked at the damage. The IFA said they found out about the damage on Tuesday morning. The damage happened on Monday night.

22-year-old Charlie Sumner has been banned for three years from football grounds. after running onto the field topless and doing somersaults at his first game at the stadium. Sumner, 20, invaded the pitch alone at Reading's Madejski Stadium during the FA Cup quarter final replay against Bradford City last month. The Reading fan, whose team was leading 3-0 at the time, did four front flips on the pitch, landing on his back each time, before being tackled by stewards.

A BMW driver was arrested today. He was driving with five children in the car. The driver hit and killed a student who was walking to the library.

Hina Shamim, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London last night. She was just weeks before her 22th birthday.

Friends today left flowers at the place where she died. They said Miss Shamim was from Peterborough. Her friends called her “Hyena.” They said she was loved and was a very nice and lovely girl.

Hina Shamim was killed after she was hit by while she was walking a short distance from her home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter are in jail because a video showing them fighting with a high school student was posted online. Stoke City’s chief executive, Tony Scholes, hopes that they can keep Asmir Begovic, their goalkeeper, as his contract has just over 12 months to run. The Bosnia international has been linked with other clubs during his time at the Britannia Stadium, and although his current deal has just over 12 months to run, Scholes believes they can match the 27-year-old's ambitions. "Clearly Asmir is a terrific goalkeeper and we are very keen to keep him at the club," he told The Sentinel. "I think when you've got extremely good players it is only natural that there will be speculation about their future."

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was in big trouble after he was seen reading a newspaper while driving. The driver’s boss called him a “complete idiot.” A passenger on the bus recorded the event on a video and sent it to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. The video shows the driver turning the pages of the newspaper while the bus was moving. The video can be seen by scrolling down. The driver was caught reading a newspaper while driving in Auckland, New Zealand. As the bus slows to a stop at a set of traffic lights he moves his head to get a good look at one of the pages. Ritchies Coachlines boss Andrew Ritchie said he was embarrassed by the “idiot” driver’s actions.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says defender Winston Reid will be ready to play in Saturday’s game against Leicester City. However, Enner Valencia will not be available. Reid has been out since March 4, when he hurt his hamstring in a 1–0 loss to Chelsea. He returned to full training during the international break. Valencia missed West Ham’s last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of a strange toe injury he suffered at home in mid-M March. Allardyce says Valencia still not match fit.

Five days before his wedding to his college sweetheart, Brittany Huber, John Redman was in a terrible car crash on a highway in Georgia. Huber died, but Redman was badly hurt and almost died. Redman lived, but his body was badly broken. His doctors said he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and would have to use a wheelchair. The future looked very bad for the 25-year-old assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, but Redman did recover against very hard odds, and on March 24 he helped lead his team to a championship title.

Lucas, pictured with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard on the left, played in a charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a Brazilian midfielder, wants to return to his best form after recovering from an injury. He had 16 starts in 19 games from late November, which helped the team’s results improve, until a groin injury in February’s Merseyside derby made him miss 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the loss to Manchester United just before the international break, their first league loss since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday’s All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Do you tired of boring father-daughter photos? One photographer has found a fun, even if a bit strange, way to make them more interesting. Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama's new series of photos shows serious-looking teenagers standing next to their fathers who are jumping in the air. In each picture the daughter looks directly into the camera smiling while her father makes a dramatic pose. A series of images by photographer Yûki Aoyama shows fathers jumping in the air next to their daughters. The images are from the 37-year-old's latest book which roughly translates into Daughter and Salary Man.

The police are looking for a man who is between 50 and 60 years old. He is suspected in a bank robbery that happened in broad daylight, and he ran away with £3,000 in cash. Morocco was removed from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments. and was fined $1 million by the CAF. The CAF also asked for another $9 million in compensation. because Morocco left as the host due to fears about the Ebola disease. Morocco was the host of the African Cup of Nations. The Ivory Coast won the tournament in Equatorial Guinea. Morocco can now play in the next two African Cup of Nations. after the first ban was given.

Tom Boyd thinks that Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has gone so well that he will be ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would be bad for Ronny Deila, who wants to keep the young Belgian player for another year, but Boyd sees a good side too. The former Celtic captain thinks Denayer’s growth can be a great example to encourage more young talents to take their next career step at Parkhead. Young defender Jason Denayer (left) has impressed on loan at Celtic this season . The 19-year-old recently won his first international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus .

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, and he said that the people who criticized him, like Paul Merson, gave him the motivation to do well in Italy. This has been a confusing season for the 33-year-old, who hasn’t reached the same level he did when he first started playing for the national team. England manager Roy Hodgson has still believed in the Tottenham player, and Townsend showed his thanks with an amazing performance at the Juventus Stadium. The Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought a 20 share of the Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The deal was approved at a special meeting on Tuesday. Wanda Madrid Investment’s legal team signed the purchase of 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to approve it. Wanda Group’s chairman, Wang Jianlin, wants to make Atletico Madrid more well known in Asia. Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, talks to the news reporters.

Antonio Conte says that his return to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 tie with England brought up “very fond memories,”, despite reports that he received death threats in the days leading up to the friendly. Conte, the former Juventus manager, replaced Cesare Prandelli as Italy’s boss in August after the Azzurri’s World Cup group-stage exit last summer, but his first seven months in charge of the national team have been topsy-turvy. Italy required a late goal from Eder to rescue a 2-2 draw against Bulgaria last Saturday and Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 216 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibernian’s easy schedule could help them pass Rangers for second place in the last month of the Championship season. His team, Dumbarton, has played both of his former teams in the league this season and will do so once again in the final weeks of the campaign. But while Stuart McCall's men have the momentum at present - beating Hibs and Cowdenbeath while Alan Stubbs' men also lost to Raith - Murray wouldn't be surprised to see the balance of power swing back towards Easter Road before long. Dumbarton boss Ian Murray believes that Rangers will struggle to maintain their pace through the run-in.

Simon Mignolet, the goalkeeper for Liverpool, took a photo with pilots inside an airplane cockpit. He was flying back to England after playing for Belgium in the Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. Mignolet was chosen to play in both games by coach Marc Wilmots, but he did not get the chance to add to his 14 international caps in either, with Chelsea stopper Thibaut Courtois preferred instead. Mignolet posted the pictures of himself in the cockpit on his official Facebook account on Wednesday.

Chyknell Hall Estate, a large country property near Bridgnorth in Shropshire, is for sale for £6 million. The estate covers 200 acres and includes a Grade II-listed man house, five cott ages, a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and a cricket pitch. The main house, Chyknell Hall, was built in 1814 and has 11 bedrooms. It has only been sold twice. The secluded grounds offer privacy, so the house might attract famous buyers.

Two college police officers in Dallas are suspended from their duties after a video showed them harassing four students and arresting one of them. after hitting him. The incident happened at El Centro College. Student Charles Adams recorded the video on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw what happened last Wednesday. The officers went up to the high school students while they were waiting for a bus outside the downtown Dallas campus.

Gary Locke has been made the permanent manager of Kilmarnock. he signed a three-year contract. he was 39 years old. he will speak at a press conference on Friday morning.

Locke joined the club last summer as assistant manager to Allan Johnston. he took control of the team when Johnston left the club at the start of February. Locke has lost just once in seven games since taking over at Rugby Park. Locke shakes hands with chairman Jim Mann after signing a three-year deal at the club.

This weekend, one of the biggest games in German football takes place. It is called Der Klassiker, but it is not as exciting as it used to be. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five Bundesliga titles. Bayern Munich is likely to win the title again this year. However, the two teams are far apart in the standings. Bayern Munich has 31 more points than Borussia Dortmund and is nine places ahead. The game is still very important for both teams. 14 schoolgirl Deva Joseph was stuck at London Stansted airport because easyJet won’t let her on the plane. she had two hand bags. Deva cried because she couldn’t fly home to Spain. she offered to pay for the second bag to be put in the hold but they only accept credit cards. she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one hit on the back of the head. The hit was so strong that it made a loud crack sound. John Potts fell down and died. Robson was drunk after his grandfather's funeral. He hit Potts outside a sports bar because Potts tried to stop a fight. The court said Robson has a history of violent crimes. He was sent to prison for 3 and 1/2 years for the attack outside the NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, in November last year.

Scoring a goal against your former team, and executing a perfect set-piece from training are two of the most satisfying things in football. For Notts County star Ellen White, Thursday night was a night to remember as she managed both at the same time against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, with County having been awarded a free kick on the edge of the box, Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood appeared to mess things up, the former almost running into the latter.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. They shout ““kill, stab, slash, and jab” while they perform eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: ““the daggers are fake.”

We spend about one-third of our life sleeping. But many people do not think about what their mind and body need during this rest time to feel fresh every day. The Sleep Health Foundation has released a study that says 30 percent of Australians complain about their lack of sleep on a daily basis. According to Chair Professor David Hillman, those misplaced hours of sleep must be paid back in order to be functional for the entire week. A study has outlined that 30 percent of Australians complain about their lack of sleep on a daily basis. The average adult needs around eight hours of sleep per night with a range of seven to nine.

The clip, uploaded to Facebook today, show an angry woman unleashing a racist tirade over her fence at a group of men who appear to be of African descent. The woman then appears in her neighbor's front yard branding a metal crowbar, verbal abusing the men and swinging the weapon at them. The men then pick up their own weapons and a scuffle breaks out. Valencia’s 19-year-old left back, Jose Luis Gaya, is the target of Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea. These English clubs hope to sign him away from Real Madrid this summer.
